messages.subject: Error in if (unique(ploidy(x)) == 2) { : the condition has length > 1
parts:
Hi all,

I am working with an updated dataset (added many more samples) and am trying to run the same code that worked on the previous version of the data.  However, after reading in my vcf, converting to a genlight object, and adding a column of the population codes to it, I run:

gl_SIFI <- gl.compliance.check(gl_SIFI)

And get the error:

Starting gl.compliance.check Error in if (unique(ploidy(x)) == 2) { : the condition has length > 1

When I look at number of loci with 0,1,2 alleles:

table(as.matrix(gl_SIFI))

       0        1        2
14865350   463818  1449419

I'm not really sure what it's saying the problem is in the error. Has anyone come across this one and have advice for me?

Thank so much,
May

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Error in if (unique(ploidy(x)) == 2) { : the condition has length > 1
parts:
Hi ,

 

Can you check

 

table(gl_SIFI@ploidy)

 

and see what you get there. Looks like you have not only ploidy =2 there.

 

But admittedly the compliance code needs to be rechecked as it should not give this error, rather telling you the result of the check.

 

Cheers, Bernd

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Error in if (unique(ploidy(x)) == 2) { : the condition has length > 1
parts:
Hi May,

 

Not sure which version you are using.

 

Are you on dartRverse or the soon to be legacy dartR?

 

The new vcf function should add the ploidy when loading

 

gl.read.vcf("your.vcf", mode="genotype")

 

 

This function is part of the dartR.base package

 

In case you do not want to bother simply add

 

gl_SIFI@ploidy <- as.integer(rep(2, nInd(gl_SIFI))

 

that should do the trick assuming you have a diploid species. Some vcf file verrsions (there are a few) might not have the ploidy information…

Cheers, Bernd
